newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Parana seeks to move up coffee output table.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Parana seeks to move up coffee output table.

text.p: Brazil's state of Parana hopes to move up to second place in the country's state coffee output table by the end of 1998 from its current fourth place, the state agricultural supply secretariat said in a statement.

According to State Agricultural Secretary Hermas Brandao, four million reais ($3.74 million) are being invested in intensive coffee production by the government and 70 million seedlings have already distributed to small-scale farmers.

Traditionally 2,500 coffee trees are planted per hectare but under the intensive method, the quantity of trees per hectare is no less than 6,000, reducing planting costs and increasing production, the statement said.

Parana was Brazil's largest coffee-producing state until 1975 when a severe frost practically destroyed the crop. In 1976, Parana ranked only tenth in the production table but had climbed back to fourth place in 1994 when frosts again savaged the crop and pushed the state back into eighth place.
Coffee trees are now only beginning to show signs of a full recovery from the frosts three years ago.
State production reached 1.1 million 60-kg bags last harvest but is expected to rise 54 percent to 1.7 million this year, the statement said.
